utterances.text: As for the forces of the Republic of the Serb Krajina, the Knin Krajina, the Croats did that during Operation Storm against them. And then it says here -- it is written here this was recently made public on the 14th of April, 2012, that they have these bombs, and that near Petrinja above Serb positions during Operation Storm from a MiG 21 such bombs were ejected. In the early 1990s, these bombs were obtained in the area of the former USSR.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, you clearly accept that the Croatian Army had access to the ODAB-500 fuel-air bomb, but you appear to exclude the possibility that the VRS also had access to the ODAB-500 fuel-air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I also quote a Croatian paper here as well, Mr. Ivo Pukanic is the person I quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. Let me say -- are you in a position to absolutely exclude the possibility that the VRS also had an ODAB-500 at the same time that the Croatian Army had an ODAB-500 fuel-air bomb?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I exclude that because they were opposing sides. I do exclude that. I wouldn't believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want to bring up, please, P1313.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, this document is dated the 23rd of July, 1995, and it's to the SRK corps command. Now, this refers to at the -- the manufacture at the maintenance and repair depot Hadzici of an air-bomb launcher for up to 500 kilogrammes, which is of a much higher quality than any so far?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you zoom in a bit further so the doctor can see the content.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please. I do thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a couple questions about this. First of all it talks about making a launcher at the maintenance and repair depot in Hadzici. Now, that doesn't sound like a standard production line method for producing a precise launching device, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: No. Hadzici did not manufacture launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, according to this document that's where they were creating this document which is described as being a --

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Please, I -- I'm not in a position to see this properly. Oh, yes, now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the moment why don't we collapse the English. Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Excellent. Thank you. Well, let me tell you. I did not really have any connections with Hadzici, to tell you the truth. And what is the year? Let me just take a look. '90-something -- no, it's 1995. No, at that time I was at the TOC. So I really do not have anything to do with this, but I do not exclude the possibility that that was done. I really have nothing to do with this and cannot really say anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We certainly can't exclude the possibility that the VRS was preparing a launcher for modified air-bombs much bigger than the FAB-250 or the FAB-275?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: No. No. Just a moment, please. Can I have a look at this again. It says here set up a commission --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpret's note: We can no longer hear the speaker. Can the witness kindly speak into her microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Doctor, we'll print out this document and hand it over to you. It may be easier to you. And you are kindly requested --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are requested to speak to the microphones.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes. As far as I can see, what is stated here is that technically the launcher was not approved. It had not been improved either, but it is being suggested here by way of an order that someone should issue an order to set up a commission and to see what the consumption of FAB-100 or 250 should be and then to be deployed in one of the units. So this is not only a reference to a 500 kilogramme launcher. Obviously it was not all right. Obviously it did not pass the test. Obviously it says here that it has to be checked further in terms of its function. So obviously this was not right, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: My point is simply this: On the basis of this document you are not in a position to exclude the possibility that the VRS was preparing to launch modified air-bombs much greater than the FAB-100 or the FAB-250?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: But it cannot be asserted either that that launcher had been -- well, you cannot see it from here. It was part of the intention, but you do not see from here that it had been completed. I cannot see it from here, because something else needs to be tested; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we have, please, 65 ter 24351, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 13, the doctor said the launcher had been mastered. They did not hear it or they did not understand it, so perhaps she should explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you confirm that you said the launcher had been -- had not been mastered well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is what is written here. I'm just reading what is written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. -- sorry. Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, on the screen in front of you you see a photograph of some objects. Do you -- can you tell us what those objects are?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, these objects look like some kind of bombs, and there's a man -- or, rather, two men that are doing something around them, and there's some motors on them, and that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I ask you to hazard a guess as to what kind of bomb that is? I'm referring to the bomb section.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to say here that this is a photograph from a newspaper article that speaks about the destruction of these assets, but I don't know exactly where this is or what this is. I just know that this was written in a periodical, that these assets were written about in this periodical. That is what I can say by way of my own information.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we kindly ask for the provenance of this photograph? Can Mr. Gaynor provide us with the provenance of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, we'll come to that in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, can you just look at the black part of the air-bomb. Tell us on the basis of your extensive experience approximately what weight is that air-bomb?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of the photograph, I cannot say exactly. I cannot say exactly. In relation to this man, it doesn't seem too big to me either to tell you the truth. Well, it's a photograph. I cannot say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Would you be able to tell us, for example, whether it's a 250, 275?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps 250, perhaps. That's what it looks like. But I cannot tell you exactly. I mean, you know, this is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not a technical drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I pull up, please, 65 ter number 24350. This is only available in the English language, so I'm going to tell you what it is, Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic. This is a press release from an organisation called UXB International Inc., dated January 24th, 2011, relating to the destruction in Bosnia of, among other things, F-58 areal-fuel bombs, FAB-275 and areal-fuel rocket modified bombs RFAB-275 M-91, and for the benefit of everyone, this is an English language point, Doctor, the word "areal" is spelled a-r-e-a-l, which mean pertaining to an area. Doctor you do accept now that these are FAB-275 fuel-air bombs, modified for delivery, using rockets?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just like to say something here. I have seen this article. I am familiar with this article. There are 68 pieces referred to here that are prepared to be destroyed, and since there are so many of them and Mr. Berko said that there were 50 of them and that they had been developed, what about the rest? Where are the rest? This is to say that obviously these were the ones that were not good out of the 50 that Mr. Berko mentioned that were there in the depot in Modrica or Glamoc or wherever and that they were destroyed. This is a newspaper article that I have seen. I know about this article. So there were 68 there that were destroyed. That is to say that all of those that had been manufactured, and Mr. Berko wrote here that there were 50 of them, they had been destroyed because obviously they did not yield certain results. That is my opinion about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: When I asked you to hazard a guess as to what size that bomb was you said it was probably a 250. In fact it's a 275. That's a forgivable error, would you accept?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps plus, minus 20 kilogrammes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It's a mistake that one can easily make when looking at an unexploded bomb.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It's a mistake which one can even more easily make when looking at the remnants of an exploded FAB-275?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: No. I've already explained this. If that is it as it is, and they said that it's the 68 -- I mean, I don't know that. I told you that that did not reach my desk. That means that it was done somewhere else. Maybe that is what Mr. Berko is speaking about. However, the difference is in the casing. Over here the casing cannot be -- well, you see here that it differs physically from the casing of an air-bomb. That is not -- well, this is something different. It's not an air-bomb. If it were to detonate then there would have to be bigger fragments left and also this white particle would have to be found, what you see on it, but I did not find that anywhere in these reports or in this what I did. This was not found anywhere. No photograph that is even close to what is depicted here. You know what? Had it detonated, it would have had to leave larger fragments, say this big, like this piece of paper or half of it, but none of that was found on the ground on the basis of the reports that I looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, I put it to you that somebody looking at the exploded remains of a FAB-275 modified air fuel bomb could very well actually mistake that for a FAB-250 areal bomb filled with a fuel-air mix, by areal in this sense I mean by a air-bomb.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: You believe that there could have been a confusion between an air-bomb and this if somebody is looking at it? If somebody is looking at fragments? No. No way. That could not have happened. Why? Because as I said a moment ago, an air-bomb, a FAB-250, it has thicker walls, if you will, and these thick walls cannot be broken by a central charge. That is to say it is impossible for a FAB-250 with trotyl to be filled with these containers with this FAE explosives. I mean, this is just a newspaper article. It was written just like that in a rather sensationalist manner. But you cannot see that here. You cannot see the same form of a warhead as in the case of a 250 warhead. The difference is considerable.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You're --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender photograph and the press release at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll admit them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Dr. Andjelkovic --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- will be assigned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, just a second. Shall we give the number now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P6052, and the article 24350 shall be assigned Exhibit P6053. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: While we're on this point, Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, you referred in your evidence in chief to the fact that fuel-air bombs are usually delivered using a parachute in order to allow the aeroplane to escape the danger zone before detonation of the fuel-air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, a parachute in that kind of environment would unquestionably be tested with the intention that the bomb be dropped from an aircraft onto the ground; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Everything that is put into weaponry, parachutes included, I mean, I assume this is done by any army, JNA included, yes, it has to be tested.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And do you accept that parachute tested in that kind of environment is therefore tested for a vertical drop? It is not tested with the intention that the air-bomb be used as a surface-to-surface weapon describing a parabola from the point of firing to the point of impact? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, the point from where it is fired on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: My point is this --

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The parachute on a fuel-air bomb is not designed to be used in a surface-to-surface configuration, is it?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, I really cannot give you an accurate answer to that. It's used from a plane, but as for ground to ground, surface to surface, I really could not say. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to call up now, please, 1D25159.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This is a report authored by Zorica Subotic in co-operation with you and Mile Poparic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can we go, please, to page 43 in English and page 45 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, do you accept veracity of the report that you co-authored?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, the page numbers are page 43 in English and page 45 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will I accept what?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you accept the veracity of that report?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes, I accept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to read out a portion of it says: "Several years before the war broke out in BiH, the Pretis factory began developing FAB-275 fuel-air bombs. Just before the start of the war in BH, production of the first 60 bombs was completed, but due to the war beginning they were not tested. During the war, a number of these bombs were fitted with four Grad rocket motors each." Now, I would like to put to you a few conclusions that we can draw from that. The first is that Pretis had the ability before the war even started to produce FAB-275 fuel-air bombs.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: That is what Mr. Berko wrote, that 50 were produced in 1990 or 1991. Whether he was correct in the figure, whether it was really 50, I cannot go into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think -- I think it's common ground essentially that Pretis had the capacity, the technical capacity, to create fuel-air bombs. It did, in fact, create fuel-air bombs. A number of those fuel-air bombs were fitted with Grad rockets, and those bombs were used during the conflict even though they had not been properly tested.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I did not see in the report any evidence about that, any evidence that they were produced. I told you that that never passed my desk in the Technical Testing Centre, because in 1991, 1992, the JNA was still in existence, and if it had been done in those years, it would have, I believe, passed my desk, but I never saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I'm not sure if Doctor is aware that this is part of her report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll -- can we go to page 1 of this report in English and B/C/S. Thank you, Mr. President, for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You confirm that we are looking at your report?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's a part of my report that I wrote in co-operation with my colleagues, but probably -- yes, this is my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And you accept --

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: But this passage that was inserted was done without my knowledge. I'm not denying it. I'm not saying I don't accept. I just overlooked it. It passed me by.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see that if perhaps this is a quotation from some other paper? Where are the sources for this? Can we see the footnotes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, then it is for -- that matter is something you should take up in your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I think your evidence, Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, on fuel-air bombs is that they have a much thinner casing than a conventional air-bomb. That's your position.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So a weapon which is designed as a fuel-air bomb such as the FAB-275 cannot be used as a conventional weapon, I assume you accept.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course it cannot be used as a conventional weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: You cannot --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can we deduce then that the FAB-275 fuel-air bomb was exclusively a fuel-air bomb and not a conventional bomb?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: We can deduce that, but we can also deduce -- we can also conclude, in fact, that fragments of it have not been found or recorded in these reports that I studied.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I pull up please P2652.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: As you see, Doctor, this is documents dated 17th of November, 1994, and it is type signed by Ratko Mladic. It states under the paragraph marked 1: "A vehicle with launcher for launching FAB-275 is to be sent immediately to the Pretis enterprise. "Once the launcher is available, the crew is to report to Major Krsmanovic latest by 0830 hours on 18 November 1994." You accept that this shows that the FAB-275 was, in fact, employed by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: From this we can only see that they prepared it, not that they launched it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I call up, please, P1296.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 19th of April, 1995, and it appears to be addressed to the command of the 27th Logistics Base and Pretis holding company, and it comes from the centre for logistics of the VRS Main Staff. If you look down the document, you can see in the second last typewritten line there is a reference to six units of the FAB-275, and a little below that you can see handwriting which says "FAB-275." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see FAB-100. That much I can see. And there is also -- it's good now. FAB-250 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: When I click it, it's moving. I suppose, so there is also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please do not click it. We have printed it out again for you. It is coming to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, you can see that in this document the VRS Main Staff has ordered Pretis to begin producing adapters and slides for all of these air-bombs, including the FAB-275, which we know to be a fuel-air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that the document I've just been given? "For their completion" it says, so that three be built into one FAB and then the amount of motors needed for their completion. FAB-275, six pieces. "Their transport for completion will be regulated later."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, I put it to you on the basis of the document you've seen that you are not in a position to exclude the possibility that the VRS used FAB-275 air -- fuel-air bombs in the Sarajevo area, are you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I exclude that possibility because I've never seen evidence of it. Why? Because I never saw those white markings or the thin casings or the burnt fragments. None of that is recorded in the Berko Zecevic report. Based on that, I can say they were not used. As far as the rest is concerned, I haven't seen anything but the two reports of my colleague Berko Zecevic, and based on that I can say that I have never encountered the use of FAB-275.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I just want to clarify the nature of your knowledge and expertise. You've clarified that you are an expert exclusively in the explosive properties of substances that explode, including fuel-air and TNT.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: As an explosive expert, I am familiar with phenomena of explosives, not only the classical one, TNT, but also liquid explosives, because I've had occasion to see on site what it looks like when I studied the causes and effects of explosions of natural gas in a house, and I did that not once but several times. So I am familiar with the effects of gas explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, can I ask you, have you ever in fact filled an empty FAB-250 bomb casing with a fuel-air mix and attempted to explode it?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're asking. Did I personally fill a FAB-250 and tested it? Could you please clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's my question. Have you personally been involved or heard of the testing of a FAB-250 bomb casing filled with a fuel-air mix, anywhere, any time?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Your question -- I'm sorry, but I do have to clear up what, in fact, you're asking. Is the casing of FAB-250 -- or, rather, was that casing filled with fuel-air explosive, or did I see that? I really don't understand the question. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Let's go through this fairly -- fairly swiftly, hopefully, you were aware that Pretis produced large quantities of the FAB-250 air-bomb; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was in its production programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you accept that Pretis would have had within its stocks large quantities of empty FAB-250 bomb casings?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: No. Pretis never had empty casings. And not just Pretis. It's not the practice to stock empty casings. They are immediately filled with trotyl and stored. Why? Because trotyl has the capacity to remain stable for ten or so years, and there's no need to keep -- to stock empty casings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, your evidence has focused on the question of whether TNT could have been removed from a 250 casing and fuel-air mix could have been inserted instead, and I'm asking you to consider an alternative scenario where you take an empty 250 casing and you fill it with fuel-air mix.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, now I understand. No, that's impossible for purely physical reasons. I said a moment ago that the casings are of different thickness. The middle part of the explosive is in too small an amount to be able to break through the casing of an air-bomb, so that this possibility, to the best of my knowledge, does not exist. How could you fill that casing with fuel-air explosive? You would have to add a container inside. It could not be filled directly with fuel-air charge. It's really an improbable situation. You would need to fill one container and put it in another container, or devise a container in the same shape as the casing and then hermetically place it inside. This does not sound logical or acceptable to me. No, I don't think that would have been possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, I'm entering the final phase of my questions, but I simply want to put it to you that you are not in a position to exclude the possibility that the VRS took empty FAB-250 casings, may have filled them with a fuel-air mix, and may have used fuel-air mix within an empty FAB-250 casing. You have not provided any evidence to exclude that possibility?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I have said a moment ago the thinnest 10 millimetre casing, and there are also those of 20 millimetres, cannot be broken by a charge like that, which is just 10 per cent of the whole mass. It does not have the strength to break through that casing. It was impossible to fill such a casing with fuel-air explosives. That's all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And as for the breaking of the bomb, we don't know if your theory is correct because nobody's ever done that experiment in your weapons facility to your knowledge. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: You know, theory guides experiments. All my knowledge about the strength, the force of this explosive, this -- this explosive is relatively weak compared to trotyl. Physically it is really impossible to fill those casings with fuel-air explosive, to operate it that way. It is just from the point of view of physics impossible because of the thickness of the casing, because of the force of the explosive, because of the way it would have to be packed inside. It cannot be placed directly into the casing. I don't know. It sounds completely inconceivable to me, illogical, and impossible ultimately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: My last few questions on this. You were -- you can answer this just with a yes or a no. You were in Belgrade for the duration of the conflict in Bosnia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You have never had an opportunity to inspect any unexploded modified air-bombs that landed in Sarajevo during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. Of course I had no occasion to see them with my own eyes, but you can make conclusions based on --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You did not have the opportunity to inspect any remnants from exploded air-bombs either?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I did see exploded bombs on the testing ground, a large number of them. Exploded in what sense? Of course I saw their effect, the fragments --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, I'll modify my question. You did not inspect any remnants of exploded modified air-bombs fired onto Sarajevo, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I couldn't, because I wasn't in Sarajevo in 1995, and these reports that were written, I look at the reports. I looked at all the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Doctor -- Doctor, as I said, you can answer these with a yes or a no as the case may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just one -- let's clarify one of her answers. Doctor, you said that you didn't have any occasion to see the unexploded modified air-bombs with your own eyes, but you could make conclusion based on what? It was not reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Based on documents. But let me just say one thing here. It's not an issue of unexploded bombs, because when they're unexploded, you can see all of it. When it's exploded, you can only see the destruction. I don't understand the question about unexploded bombs. I've never seen them, and in the reports I only read about exploded bombs, one FAB-100 and one FAB-250 that Mr. Zecevic keeps mentioning in his reports, but he never tested that explosive to make sure that it's indeed the explosive he claims was inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, in your report you analyse a great number of specific incidents. Is it correct that you did not carry out a site visit to any of those incident sites?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: That's correct. I did not. It's in Sarajevo. I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It follows that you did not personally have access to or test any of the material gathered from those incident sites?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: This report written by Mr. Berko was written in 2007. That other report was written in 1995. In both reports, there are a lot of inconsistencies that Mr. Berko himself, who was on the site, recorded inconsistencies in his 2007 report. So based on his report and the other reports of -- that were written and all the photographs, I could conclude what it was all about without going to the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And you did not interview any persons who were present at the incident sites at the times of those incidents?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I said I didn't. I only studied both reports in Belgrade. I had no personal contacts in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we need to have a break or would you like to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will need 15, perhaps 20 minutes. Maybe we should have a break before that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long do you think you need for your re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not more than 15 to 20 minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then shall we break for 15 minutes in order to conclude a bit earlier than usual?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was advised to take at least 20 minutes' break. We will resume at 25 past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, can you tell the Trial Chamber whether there are any other lethal weapons that are fuel rocketed within the armament of Yugoslavia? What kind of rockets are there?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I really wouldn't know that. I can't tell you because that is not within my purview. There are rockets such as the one on the M-84 tank, but that's a cannon ammunition. There are also zoljas. There are Osas, but that's beyond the scope of my expertise. I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly what kind of rockets there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a Grad rocket as well as a Luna rocket?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Globally speaking, what does a rocket of that kind consist of?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: It has a warhead and it has a motor that propels it to a certain target. That's as much as I know as a technical expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Of these two parts, which part is your concern?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Only the warhead with explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who is the one that tests the propellants?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: They are tested by people who are concerned with propellants, either gunpowder or other types of fuel. This is a special profession, a special line expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You never tested anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: No. No, that was not what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked whether you ever tested modified air-bombs, and you said that such modified air-bombs has never appeared on your table. Could you please be more precise? What would it be that would be modified in a bomb of that kind?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: If you consider that a modified bomb, which is a bomb with liquid charge and an explosive charge, if that is what you consider when you say a modified bomb, I've never seen any such thing, and I have never tested any such thing. I've never reviewed documents to see whether everything is according to standards. I had never encountered such assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that a bomb with rocket motors is a modified bomb?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: That doesn't have to be the case. Although the answer would be yes. How shall I put it? Artillery weapons that I'm familiar with as a result of my profession have warheads and have rocket propellants, and if such an air-bomb has a rocket propellant, it can also be considered as a modified bomb, but only in those terms. That would be the only element, the rocket motor that is attached to it. It cannot be considered as a modified bomb if the only thing that differs is the kind of explosive in it. Then it's an entirely different thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you ever asked -- was there any need for you to test the well-known air-bomb in which the only thing that was changed was propellant?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: There was no need to test an air-bomb that has already been tested, because all the fragments for its construction, which means all the elements of its construction starting with the body, the detonator, the explosive, all that exists in the construction documents, and every time when a new bomb was manufactured, all those elements had to be respected.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we look at 1D25159. The Serbian page that I want is 43. I don't know whether the English page was the same. We saw that document only awhile ago. The Serbian page 45, and I don't know whether the English page corresponds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this passage, it says that there were some bombs FAB-275. Could you please read the last sentence and could you read it aloud.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: "In December 2011, 58 FAB-275 aircraft bombs were destroyed in Glamoc. These rockets had been fitted onto 24 bombs. So out of the 60 FAB-275 aircraft bombs produced, 58 were destroyed in 2011 while no more than two were used in the war, and neither of these two bombs were used in Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you adhere by the claims in this report?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, because in the report that I drafted I never said that there were aerosol bombs in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I'd like to call up P6052. It's a P document, P6052. The record is correct. Can we zoom in on the tail fins. Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, have you ever encountered such remains in the documents that you studied and reviewed? Have you ever encountered such remains of an air-bomb that was launched in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I've already told you that I have not encountered any such things in the documents that I reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What would these motors be, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Really, I can't tell you. I'm not familiar with these motors, so I wouldn't be able to tell you what kind of motors these are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not going to ask you to speculate, although Mr. Gaynor did ask you to speculate. The central barrel, could it contain a parachute? Could this be an original fuel-air bomb?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Really, it's very difficult to say that based on a photo. I would be speculating, whatever I told you. I really can't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Just one more question in that respect. Did you know -- do you know that before the war and during the war in Republika Srpska whether there were some testing grounds where artillery weapons could be tested and where rockets could be tested as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: The JNA had a lot of testing grounds in the former Yugoslavia. There were some in Macedonia, and there were some in Bosnia-Herzegovina as well. In Bosnia-Herzegovina, there's a large testing ground known as Kalinovik. Its equipment was modest, but the conditions there were quite good for testing artillery ammunition. That's where they tested tank ammunition, 125 millimetres. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're talking about things that happened before the war.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who controlled Kalinovik during the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Kalinovik was under Muslim control, but I'm not sure. I wouldn't be able to tell you, because I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before the war was there any testing near Glamoc?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, these are some grounds -- I don't know. I just know about the big ones, Kalinovik, the ones in Macedonia, Krivolak. I know of Nikinci, then Centa was mentioned, but really, I don't know of others. That is what I know as far as these testing grounds are concerned and that's where I went myself, but for the rest --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. For your information, Kalinovik was always under our control.

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic for your contribution to these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Doctor, Judge Baird has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Doctor, in the course -- in the course of putting his case to you, Mr. Gaynor put a suggestion, and I didn't get your response. I shall repeat that suggestion for you. He put to you: "As for the breaking of the bomb, we don't know if their theory is correct, because nobody has ever done that experiment in your weapons facility to your knowledge?" Do you recollect that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the question was whether an F-250 casing can be fitted with fuel-air explosive. My answer was no, because the central charge that initiates the fuel-air, that's how it goes out, it is too weak. It cannot break this strong steel casing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that was exactly the suggestion that I was after. I shall repeat it: "As for the breaking of the bomb, we don't know if your theory is correct because nobody has ever done that experiment in your weapons facility to your knowledge?"

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: Such an experiment, that is to say to put into the casing of a FAB-250 air-bomb, to put this kind of explosive and to -- well, that would be unacceptable, let me put it that way. Let me not say anything else. It is unacceptable because in advance one knows that this casing was not meant for a fuel-air explosive because of its physical characteristics, because of the thickness of the metal and the type of steel used that has to be appropriate for trotyl.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: May I? Just one question on the basis of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Baird suggests to allow you to put that question. Yes. Please go ahead, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, a moment ago you responded to His Excellency Mr. Baird that it is well known that this is not sufficient. Now I am asking you about experience with air-bombs with classical charges that were insufficient or of poor quality or was the explosive of poor quality and what happens then?

utterances.speaker: MIRJANA ANDJELKOVIC LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to say that when there are charges with explosive, then the requirements are very strict for the quality of the explosive, because if the explosive is not good, that is to say if it has some shortcomings, cracks, and so on, there can be incomplete detonation. So one knows in advance that the explosive has to be absolutely properly put into the casing so that there would be no failure during targeting. That means, for instance, if an air-bomb was not to be exploded properly, if it could not function properly, if there could be the so-called deflagration, that is to say insufficient detonation. So that is well known and that is why this is taken into account. And also, it is therefore well known that if this kind of charge were to be put in an air-bomb, it would not yield the kind of effects that are expected. It is quite senseless to put into such a bomb that kind of explosive.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, Dr. Andjelkovic Lukic, and I appreciate your coming to The Hague to give it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There are a couple of matters I'd like to deal with now. The first thing is Prosecution's motion to exclude in part the evidence of Mirko Sosic, requesting that the Chamber order the exclusion of certain paragraphs. The accused filed his response stating that he does not oppose the motion and that he would delete the said paragraphs and relevant associated exhibits. So in light of this response, I'm wondering whether the Prosecution is minded to withdraw its motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah. We consider that a resolution, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Second issue relates to the accused's motion for videolink for Miroslav Gagovic, filed on the 12th of December. Probably today -- yes, today the Prosecution filed its response not opposing the motion. Having been satisfied with the inability of the witness to travel to The Hague due to his health condition and the relevancy of his expected testimony, the Chamber will grant the motion and instruct the Registry to take all necessary measures to implement this decision. Are there any matters to raise at the moment? Then otherwise --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 17th day of December, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.
